hypothesis: A symmetric fixed take-profit may reduce peak-profit giveback without destroying the exact aligned-entry v52 HYPE route's after-cost edge.
decision: Retain the native v52 HYPE exit and reject the tested symmetric 40-500-bps fixed-target grid. Revision 2 preserves the same economics while binding the evidence to the canonically formatted generator source.
falsifier: A predeclared independent both-side or explicitly side-specific fixed-target experiment, with source-compatible entries and executable costs, beats the native exit in total and leave-largest net return without materially degrading the opposite direction.
limitations: The fixed-entry study cannot model additional signals that an earlier target exit could free capital to take.
One-minute OHLC cannot prove intrabar target-versus-stop ordering or private IOC execution.
The later-confirmation cohort contains one long and no short, so it cannot validate a side-specific short target.
The selected 500-bps target was selected on development only and reduced total after-cost net return versus the native exit.
